clue.text: Sailors love to skylark, it's clear

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS is the plural

indicators.note: to skylark is to frolic about, so the letters of love play around into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors fooling about with love declare the coast is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to skylark' rearranges the four letters into OLVE; AB is the standard crossword abbreviation for an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them of guilt, to declare them innocent.

clue.text: Man devoured by lion, perhaps-a circus performer

indicators.note: something devoured by another ends up inside it

parts.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is eaten by a big cat at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoured by' sets the man's name inside the big cat; the leading A is the clue's own 'a', which looks attached to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or trapeze artist in the big top is a gymnastic entertainer.

clue.text: Survey the whole lot with a girl

parts.note: a sum is the total, the whole lot
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone looks over everything with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey as a noun is a general overview or brief account.

clue.text: Tracks people's ancestries?

explanation.definitionFit: Railway lines are tracks; family lines are lineages of descent.

clue.text: Under a spell and thence transformed

indicators.note: transformed tells us the letters change shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was bewitched and then changed form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges AND THENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewitched by magic is the sense of being under a spell.

clue.text: Subordinate theme

explanation.definitionFit: A subject is someone under a ruler's authority, and also the topic or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Roughly licks smooth

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are handled carelessly into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat licks its fur flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges LICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick means glossy and even, like smoothed hair.

clue.text: Abominable service!

parts.note: a religious service so wicked it is literally abominable, a Satanic parody of the Eucharist

explanation.surface: A complaint about terrible service in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Satanic ritual parodying the Catholic Eucharist is an evil church service.

clue.text: It's obvious I've turned up to make an impression

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone has arrived to make their mark, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses IVE to EVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, clear.

clue.text: High toned speaker

parts.note: a loudspeaker for high-pitched sound, or a bird singing shrilly

explanation.surface: Describes a posh, refined orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loudspeaker that reproduces treble frequencies; also a chirping bird.

clue.text: Of Latin descent, from Minorca

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the island's name, reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone from a Spanish island is said to have Latin roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a light anagram signal: the seven letters of MINORCA rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanic languages and peoples are those descended from Latin and Rome.

clue.text: Fancy getting game in one move

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the instruction to move tells us to shift the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess player dreams of winning in a single move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges the two fodder words into MAGINE, set after the Roman one; the surface reads like a chess player plotting a one-move win.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something as a verb is to picture or suppose it in the mind.

clue.text: Growth of pantomime

parts.note: the plant that sprouts overnight in the Jack story, a favourite British Christmas pantomime

explanation.surface: A remark on how pantomime has flourished.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British family stage show at Christmas; Jack climbs a giant plant in one of the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant plant grown from magic beans is the central growth of the Jack pantomime.

clue.text: Used two joints on Sunday

parts.note: the two joints are knees, used when praying in church on a Sunday

explanation.surface: Someone cooked two roasts for Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' suggests the British Sunday roast meat, but they are the knees bent in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on both knees in church is the posture described.

clue.text: Sell the dummy-touchdown possible

explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is an attempt to deceive someone; in rugby a try (grounding the ball) being 'on' means a score is possible.

clue.text: Poor vision means some listeners are kept in the dark

indicators.note: are kept in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: night is the dark
ears are listeners

explanation.surface: Some people listening are left uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are kept in' places the listeners inside the dark; 'kept in the dark' looks like the idiom for uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Short sight, myopia, is defective eyesight for distant things.

clue.text: Accept later you're a chip off the old block

definitions.text: you're a chip off the old block

parts.note: to accept is to take
after means later

explanation.surface: Someone tells a child they will resemble a parent in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To resemble a parent closely is the idiom of being a chip off the old block.

clue.text: Gold sovereign?

parts.note: a sovereign is a king; the king whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.surface: Asks about an old British gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold coin; here it means a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Phrygian king whose touch turned things to gold.

clue.text: Place of refreshment for Great Dane off the leash

indicators.note: a dog off the leash runs wild, so the letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A big dog has run loose in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the leash' rearranges GREAT DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor area where tea and snacks are served is a refreshment spot.

clue.text: A climbing frame put in nursery, perhaps

definitions.text: A climbing frame put in nursery, perhaps

parts.words: A climbing frame put in nursery, perhaps
parts.note: a frame for climbing plants, sold or placed in a garden nursery

explanation.surface: Play equipment installed in a children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is a plant nursery, and the climbing is by plants, not children.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood supporting climbing plants is a garden frame.

clue.text: Normally Laura's out with a sweetheart

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of place, rearranged

parts.note: Laura's with its S counted as letters
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Laura is usually out with a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAURAS into ASARUL; 'sweetheart' is the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally, usually, is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Abuse uncommon parlance

explanation.definitionFit: To slang someone is to hurl insults at them; slang is also informal, non-standard speech.

clue.text: Loan may be arranged, though it's irregular

indicators.note: be arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A loan can be fixed up, though not by the usual rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be arranged' rearranges LOAN MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something deviating from the norm, an oddity.

clue.text: Turned into a dreadful tragedy

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Things changed into a terrible disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges TRAGEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrated means spun or revolved.

clue.text: Hack returns, writing for the papers

indicators.note: returns means the word for hack is read from right to left

parts.note: to hack is to axe, chop
MS, manuscript, is writing

explanation.surface: A journalist comes back to write for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AXE into EXA. 'Hack' looks like a journalist; it is a chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers are examinations set in school, as in sitting a paper.

clue.text: Splendour pursued by a grim French mistress

indicators.note: pursued by means the first piece is followed by the others

parts.note: pomp is splendour
dour means grim

explanation.surface: A dazzling figure is chased by a stern French teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame de Pompadour was Louis XV's mistress; 'French mistress' suggests a schoolteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame de Pompadour was the famous royal favourite of Louis XV of France.

clue.text: A hard question for one, a sitter for another

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling problem; also one who sits or postures for a portrait.

clue.text: A mass rising on the Indian border

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd climbs a hill at India's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the mass upwards into SSAM; 'on the Indian border' fits because Assam is a frontier state of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian state in the north-east borders Bhutan and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Waiting rooms modified by long use

indicators.note: modified tells us the letters are altered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Waiting areas have changed through heavy wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges LONG USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport and hotel lounges are rooms where people sit and wait.

clue.text: Variety act ends with melody

indicators.note: variety suggests change, so the letters take a different order

explanation.surface: A variety show turn finishes on a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' rearranges ACT ENDS; it poses as music-hall entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung or played above the main tune.

clue.text: One who feels the heat for one who feels the cold

explanation.definitionFit: Someone perspiring in hot weather; a woollen jumper is worn by someone who is chilly.

clue.text: Dog that will have its day, some day perhaps!

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Every dog has its day, and this one will some day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SOME DAY; 'that will have its day' plays on the saying every dog has its day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian breed of dog.
